headline: Ghostly Cave Snail Found in Chinese Mountains Offers Clues to Hidden Ecosystems
meta_description: Scientists discover the first eyeless freshwater cave snail in China, a ghostly creature living 2,062 meters high that challenges our understanding of undergro…
summary_short: Researchers in China have identified a remarkable eyeless snail living in complete darkness high in mountain caves—the first of its kind documented in the country.
body:
Deep within a high-altitude limestone cave in Yunnan Province, scientists have discovered an entirely new species of freshwater snail that has evolved to thrive in absolute darkness. Named Erhaia dijiang after a faceless god in ancient Chinese mythology, this ghostly creature represents the first recorded eyeless cave snail ever found in China—a gap in scientific knowledge that hints at how much remains unexplored beneath East Asia. The snail, which lacks eyes entirely, sports a nearly transparent shell, unpigmented body, and long slender tentacles adapted for its subterranean world. What makes the finding particularly striking is that researchers located it at 2,062 meters elevation, making it the highest-altitude cave snail yet recorded in its family, Erhaiidae.

The species' habitat tells its own story. Living in less than a meter of water at a stable temperature near 20°C, Erhaia dijiang grazes on microscopic diatoms clinging to rocks and remains confined to its cave environment, never venturing into nearby streams even when seasonal rains flush the waters. Yet beneath this scientific triumph lies an urgent concern: the research team found only three living adults during their initial investigation in August 2025, along with a single empty shell and no juveniles whatsoever. This sparse population has prompted researchers to describe the species' conservation outlook as "far from optimistic."

The discovery underscores a broader truth—that China's underground freshwater ecosystems remain largely unmapped and poorly understood. Scientists are now calling for comprehensive investigations of cave systems throughout the country to identify additional hidden species before they disappear, highlighting how fragile these isolated underground worlds truly are.
quick_facts: First eyeless freshwater cave snail documented in China
Found at 2,062 meters elevation in Yunnan Province cave
Only three living adults discovered during initial field study
Named after faceless deity from ancient Chinese mythology
Feeds on microscopic algae in near-total darkness
